records.THE_PIN_IS_THE_SHA256: The TANGO academic download page carries NO version number -- its files are named only by platform, e.g. "Executable Tango - Linux 64bits". So the sha256 above IS the version for the purposes of PREREGISTRATION 5.2 and 12 step 4. Cite it as such. If a future download of "the same" file yields a different digest, that is a different tool and must be recorded as a separate run.

Per-residue columns: res, aa, Beta, Turn, Helix, Aggregation, Conc-Stab_Aggregation. Summary line to stdout: AGG, AMYLO, TURN, HELIX, HELAGG, BETA.
STILL_TO_BE_FILLED_BY_THE_AUTHOR.parameters_vs_bradshaw_2014: RECONCILED, AND THE MAPPING IS NOT ONE-TO-ONE. Bradshaw 2014 (PLoS ONE 9:e111196) reports "both alpha helix and beta sheet aggregation using default parameters, threshold = 5%". The local binary has NO threshold parameter and NO alpha/beta switch. Those two settings were WEB-FORM controls, and both are post-processing here: "both" means read the Aggregation column (beta) AND the HELAGG summary value (helical); "threshold = 5%" means apply a 5 percent cutoff to the output ourselves. THE REAL GAP IS "DEFAULT PARAMETERS". The command line has no defaults: nt and ct are MANDATORY (omitting them aborts), and ph/te/io/tf/stab are silently optional. The web form's defaults are therefore NOT recoverable from the binary, and must be taken from the TANGO paper or the archived form, or declared unknown. Until then our run is NOT a reproduction of Bradshaw's settings, only of the same program.

version_claim.THE_BINARY_SELF_REPORTS_NOTHING: Every version flag tried -- --version, -v, -V, --help, -h -- returns the same string, "Error when input: no peptide sequence found". The binary has no version switch and no usage message. `strings` yields no version token: the only dated strings are the compiler banner, GCC 4.1.2 20080704 (Red Hat 4.1.2-48). The download page carries no version either. So "2.3.1" is a FILENAME CLAIM, not a self-report, and is NOT independently confirmable from the artefact. The sha256 above is the only pin that is.

MEASURED_PARAMETER_SENSITIVITY_2026-11-1._how: Manual example peptide DNEWGYIAYHVSQDP, one parameter varied at a time, per-residue output files compared with cmp(1). Baseline: nt=N ct=N ph=7.4 te=303 io=0.05 tf=0 stab=-10.
MEASURED_PARAMETER_SENSITIVITY_2026-11-1.WHAT_THIS_MEANS_FOR_PREREGISTRATION: pH and temperature CHANGE THE ANSWER and must be pre-registered as fixed values before any run. stab and conc showed no observable effect on this sequence in this build -- which is a measurement on one peptide, NOT a proof that they are inert in general. Do not report them as ignored; report them as "varied, no observable effect on the test peptide".

TRAPS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT: EXIT CODE IS 0 ON FAILURE. A run with a missing N-terminal group prints "Error when input: ..." and still exits 0, writing no output file. Any batch harness MUST check that the output file exists and is non-empty, because the exit status will not tell it anything.

THE MANUAL DESCRIBES A DIFFERENT OUTPUT FORMAT FROM THE ONE THE BINARY PRODUCES. The manual lists a final column "Percentage of Helical Aggregation"; this build emits "Conc-Stab_Aggregation" instead and reports HELAGG only on the stdout summary line. The shipped manual is therefore not a description of the shipped binary.

THE MANUAL'S nt/ct DESCRIPTIONS ARE TRANSPOSED. It gives "nt: Protection at the C-terminus ... Y for amidated" and "ct: Protection at the N-terminus ... A for acetylated". Amidation is a C-terminal modification and acetylation an N-terminal one, so either the names or the descriptions are swapped. We use nt=N ct=N (no protection at either end), which is unaffected by the ambiguity -- but ANY protected-terminus run must resolve this first.
The output file is written to the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY, named <identifier>.txt, and silently overwrites. Distinct identifiers per run, or a fresh directory per run.
Maximum sequence length is 20000 aa (string found in the binary). DISC1 at 854 and TRIOBP-1 at 652 are far inside it; no chunking needed, so no window-boundary artefact from chunking.

_MODERN_ARM_STATUS_2026-11-16._rule: PREREGISTRATION 5.2 admits a modern predictor only if it is version-pinnable AND runs locally. Tested by fetching the repositories, not by reading catalogue entries.

AggreProt.verdict: NOT ADMISSIBLE TODAY -- cannot be run locally.
AggreProt.why: The README instructs "unzip nnap-data.zip" and never says where nnap-data.zip comes from. It is not in the GitHub repository (11 .py files, setup.py, LICENSE, README, .internal_commit.txt) and cannot be in the Zenodo v1.0 archive, which is 22.9 kB in total. Without it there are no model weights and no Atomic.csv.
AggreProt.paper_data_availability_verbatim: "Aggreprot is freely available and accessible at https://loschmidt.chemi.muni.cz/aggreprot/." -- a SERVER availability statement. The paper has no code-availability and no model-availability statement. [READ, NAR 2024 52:W159-W169, version of record]
AggreProt.guessed_weight_urls_all_returned_200_tex: Three guessed URLs for nnap-data.zip returned HTTP 200, 0 bytes, text/html -- the SPA catch-all, not a file. THIRD independent instance in this project of "a status code is not reachability".

licence_CONFLICT_THREE_SOURCES.which_governs: The repository LICENSE governs the code. NC and ShareAlike are not formalities here and need a deliberate decision before publication.

AggreProt.how_to_unblock: Email the corresponding authors (addresses printed in the paper) for nnap-data.zip and its checksum. Until then record as UNAVAILABLE, not as a failure -- the same treatment ProA receives.
AggreProt.RELEVANT_TO_H4: AggreProt is explicitly a WINDOW SCANNER: sequences are "fragmented into overlapping hexapeptides using a six-amino-acid windows shifted one amino acid at a time", scored by an ensemble of five DNNs, then "aggregated (averaged) per residue by a sliding window procedure". [READ, p. W161] That is exactly the architecture H4 is about.

AggrescanAI.runs_locally_because: Read cell by cell: apart from #@param form annotations, which are COMMENTS and inert outside Colab, it is ordinary Python (requests, pandas, torch, transformers, tensorflow.keras, numpy, plotly). Nothing is Colab-specific. Porting is mechanical.
AggrescanAI.NOT_REPRODUCIBLE_AS_WRITTEN: Weights are fetched from huggingface.co/alvaro-2/aggrescanai/resolve/MAIN -- a moving branch head -- and ProtT5 via from_pretrained() with NO revision= argument. Both resolve to whatever is current on the day of the run. A silent upstream update would change our numbers with nothing in the output to show it. This is TANGO's missing version again, and worse: downloaded bytes cannot change under us, a branch head can.

FREE_PARAMETERS_THAT_MUST_BE_PREREGISTER.window_size: Smoothing is a user slider, default 7, range 1-25, and changing it changes the profile. RECOMMENDATION: report the RAW column `aggrescanai_score`, which is unsmoothed, and fix the threshold instead -- the parameter then does not exist.
FREE_PARAMETERS_THAT_MUST_BE_PREREGISTER.edge_artefact: The smoother is np.convolve(..., mode="same"), which ZERO-PADS at the termini. The first and last window_size//2 residues are biased downward by construction, not by biology -- 3 residues at each end at the default. A second reason to prefer the raw column.

CIRCULARITY_QUESTION_OPEN._STATUS: CLOSED 16 Nov 2026 -- CONFIRMED, AND WORSE THAN THE FILENAME SUGGESTED.
CIRCULARITY_QUESTION_OPEN._evidence_grade: READ. Navarro et al. (2026) J Mol Biol 438:169643, version of record, full PDF opened. Supersedes the earlier inference from the model filename.
CIRCULARITY_QUESTION_OPEN.confirmed_verbatim: "We used the Curated Protein Aggregation Database (CPAD) 2.0 [22] ... The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets. The training subset (80%) has 75,524 total residues, of which 2,167 correspond to APR+ positions."
CIRCULARITY_QUESTION_OPEN.the_shipped_model_is_the_CPAD90_ensemble: "Models trained on the CPAD90 dataset showed significant improvement ... Consequently, the final predictive model corresponds to the ensemble trained on the CPAD90 dataset using optimized hyperparameters, from now on called AggrescanAI." This matches the shipped weight filenames cpad_hotidp90_model_cv_1..5.h5 exactly: CPAD + HoTIDP homology transfer at the 90% threshold.
CIRCULARITY_QUESTION_OPEN.THE_CONTAMINATION_SURFACE_IS_WIDER_THAN_: CPAD90 is CPAD "together with homologous sequences", built by homology transfer through the HoTIDP server using OrthoInspector and OmaDB orthologues. SO IT IS NOT SUFFICIENT TO CHECK THAT A BENCHMARK PROTEIN IS ABSENT FROM CPAD. An ORTHOLOGUE of a CPAD protein can carry a transferred APR annotation into the training set. Any row of regions.json whose protein is homologous to a CPAD entry is potentially training data for AggrescanAI.
CIRCULARITY_QUESTION_OPEN.WE_CANNOT_CHECK_IT_FROM_PUBLISHED_FILES: The paper's entire data-availability statement is "Data will be made available on request." The CPAD90 membership list is therefore NOT public. CPAD 2.0 itself is public, so CPAD membership is checkable; the homology-expanded set is not, short of asking the authors or extracting Supplementary Table 2.
CIRCULARITY_QUESTION_OPEN.the_authors_knew_and_said_so: "A crucial consideration is that the predictor was trained on datasets that, even with augmentation, currently encompass a restricted subset of experimentally validated Aggregation-Prone Regions (APRs)."

PUBLISHED_PERFORMANCE_READ_THE_MARGIN_BE._source: Navarro 2026 Figure 2, ROC on the external AmyPro validation set [READ].
PUBLISHED_PERFORMANCE_READ_THE_MARGIN_BE.WHAT_THIS_MEANS: The best modern sequence predictor scores AUROC 0.69 on an external benchmark, and the structure-aware Aggrescan3D scores 0.51 -- indistinguishable from random. NO CONFIDENCE INTERVALS ARE GIVEN for any of these. CLAUDE.md rule 2 applies directly: before we spend anything on separating two predictors, note that the published gap between the best modern tool and the 2007 legacy tool is 0.69 vs 0.58, reported without error bars, on a benchmark the same paper calls inadequate. A benchmark of ours that aims to resolve differences smaller than that needs its power argued first.
PUBLISHED_PERFORMANCE_READ_THE_MARGIN_BE.AND_IT_IS_SELF_ASSESSED: This ranking is reported by the authors of the winning tool, on a benchmark set they constructed. It is not independent.

licence_and_reuse.paper: Elsevier, NOT open access. The PDF states: "All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies."

_MODERN_ARM_STATUS_2026-11-16.CONSEQUENCE_FOR_5.2_AUTHORS_CALL: As of today the modern arm is ONE tool, not two. A single-tool modern arm weakens a headline question that is about a GENERATION of predictors. Options, to be registered before scoring: wait for the AggreProt weights, widen the arm to another version-pinnable local tool, or register explicitly that the modern arm is one tool and say so in the title.
_MODERN_ARM_STATUS_2026-11-16.NOTHING_WAS_RUN: Executing either tool on a dataset protein before the freeze would breach the pre-registration. Note that AggrescanAI's own example sequence is UniProt P37840, alpha-synuclein, WHICH IS A ROW IN data/regions.json -- so even its demo cannot serve as a smoke test. Use an unrelated sequence.
